newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mitterrand widow, illegitimate daughter at grave.
newsitem.headline: Mitterrand widow, illegitimate daughter at grave.

text.p: Danielle and Mazarine, widow and illegitimate daughter of Francois Mitterrand, stood side-by-side at the late French president's grave on Saturday as friends and family marked the first anniversary of his death.
Mazarine's mother, museum curator Anne Pingeot, was absent, although she attended Mitterrand's funeral a year ago.
The private life of Mitterrand, France's Socialist president from 1981 to 1995, was in headlines through the week as friends and foes recalled his last moments.
Mitterrand suffered from cancer of the prostate which he hid from the public through most of his time in office. It killed him at age 79, less than a year after he ended his second term.

Some newspapers predicted his private life would soon be highlighted again by publication in France of the memoirs of a Scandinavian journalist hinting she was Mitterrand's mistress through the last years of his life.

A message from German Chancellor Helmut Kohl was read at Mitterrand's hometown graveside in southwest France. It called him "a great Frenchman, a great European and a dear friend I will never forget."
